interpretation: Instruction: take the finished print off the 3D printer's build plate, put it on the black shelf, and leave the build plate on the printer. Objects (perception ids at the start): obj5 = the print, an orange hexagonal prism with a raised blue disc on top (flat-to-flat 4.43 cm, corner-to-corner 5.1 cm, body 1.4 cm tall plus a ~2.3 mm disc of ~2 cm diameter), centred at (0.0748, -0.3578), flat normals at about -4.5/55.5/-64.5 deg. obj4 = the black build plate, 19x19x1 cm, top at z=0.0846, footprint x -0.025..0.165, y -0.471..-0.28. obj6 = the black shelf, a 24x13x6 cm black box in front of the printer, top at z=0.065, x 0.17..0.30, y -0.496..-0.255. obj1/obj2/obj3 = the printer body, its gantry beam and its Z column (column at x -0.08..0, y -0.247..-0.207, up to z 0.365). Goal state: the print resting on obj6's top surface, and the plate still seated on the printer bed, unmoved. Ambiguity: the print's orientation on the shelf is not specified.
plan: Initial plan: grasp the print across a pair of flats, lift it, carry it to the shelf centre (0.235, -0.376) and set it down level. A pure top-down grasp at this ~37 cm radius was only reachable at grasp height (joint5 at its 1.22 rad limit), and there the forearm (link3) was 1.3 cm into the printer column's top corner. So I tilted the approach 25 deg toward azimuth -140 deg, which shifts the wrist toward +x, turns the arm plane away from the column, and stays reachable from z 0.11 to 0.16. Placing would use the same tilt with the yaw turned to about -95 deg. Changes along the way: (1) the TCP landed 6-10 mm off target. I found a per-joint deadband (each joint stops short of its target in the direction of motion, 0.030 rad on joints 5 and 6) and compensated by commanding goal + deadband*sign(dq). (2) The first close (25 deg tilt) rode up over the print, so I retried at a 15 deg tilt. (3) That close also rode up and only pinched the blue disc, and the pinch could not lift the print, so I switched to pushing. (4) Pushing from behind (-x) was impossible because the forearm hits the column (4.5-6.6 cm penetration), and dragging via the disc pinch slipped at once. (5) Final strategy: straddle the print with the open gripper (closing axis along the push), keep the fingertips ~3 mm above the plate, and sweep 14 cm along -30 deg so the rear finger pushes the print off the plate's front edge onto the shelf. Then push 4 cm further onto the shelf and retreat.

steps.what: Read the robot, cameras and objects; fitted the hexagon from top-face points; checked IK and collisions for top-down and tilted grasps; mapped reachability over tilt/yaw and heights; checked shelf placement reach.
steps.why: Identify the print, plate and shelf, and find an arm pose that reaches the print without hitting the printer column.
steps.result: Chose approach tilt 25 deg toward azimuth -140 deg: reachable z 0.11-0.16, ~2.2 cm forearm clearance, no arm contacts. Step 0.

steps.what: Moved home -> pre-grasp 3 cm above the grasp (4 s).
steps.why: Get above the print with the open fingers straddling it.
steps.result: Done at step 64. The TCP stopped ~6 mm off target (joint5 1.7 deg short).

steps.what: Measured the real fingertips in the scene-camera point cloud.
steps.why: The finger collision spheres reach 3.4 cm and I didn't trust the nominal 2 cm tip reach.
steps.result: The tips reach ~2.45 cm past the TCP, and the lowest finger point at 25 deg tilt is ~2.5 cm below the TCP. Raised the grasp height from 0.112 to 0.114 so the tips don't touch the plate.

steps.what: Descended to the grasp pose with a constant-offset correction.
steps.why: Put the fingers beside the print near plate height.
steps.result: Step 98. The TCP was 1 cm off-centre along the closing axis (one finger against the print). A 0.5 s hold (step 106) showed no settling. The joint comparison showed every joint stops short of its target in the direction of motion (j1-j4 0.15-0.4 deg, j5/j6 1.73 deg).

steps.what: Deadband-compensated re-centring move (command FK(q_goal + dead*sign(q_goal - q_now))).
steps.result: Step 128. TCP within 0.5 mm of the goal, centred on the print. The compensation worked for every later move (errors under 0.5 mm).

steps.why: Grasp the print across its sides.
steps.result: Step 143. Reading 0.9685 (closed_empty): missed. The fingers rode up over the print's top edge, pushing the TCP up 5.6 mm, and closed above it. Print and plate unmoved.

steps.what: Lifted 1.5 cm, opened, re-fitted the print; re-grasped with a 15 deg tilt (yaw -145) so the whole fingertip edge sat 4-6 mm below the print's top, tips ~1-3 mm above the plate.
steps.why: With the 25 deg tilt only one low finger corner overlapped the 1.4 cm side.
steps.result: Steps 162-229. Positioned within 0.4 mm, fingers straddling the print at plate height (image 030).
Step 244. Reading 0.7336, gap 1.86 cm. The fingers again rode up (TCP +3.1 mm) and pinched the blue disc on top. The print tilted ~5 deg.

steps.what: Test lift 5 mm, then 1.5 cm more.
steps.why: Check whether the disc pinch could carry the print, and whether the plate came with it.
steps.result: Step 263: one side of the print lifted (tilting); the plate stayed put. Step 289: the pinch slipped (reading 0.998) and the print fell back flat onto the plate, unharmed.

steps.what: Evaluated pushing from behind (-x) with several push directions, tilts and yaws.
steps.why: Grasping looked hopeless for this short part with these fingers.
steps.result: Rejected: at every start pose behind the print, the forearm (link3) is 4.5-6.6 cm into the printer column.

steps.what: Re-created the disc pinch (step 361) and dragged 14 cm along -25 deg, turning the yaw from -145 to -105 deg.
steps.why: The pinch blocks the disc along the closing axis, so dragging near that axis might slide the print.
steps.result: Step 463. The pinch was lost at once; the print moved less than 1 cm and stayed on the plate.

steps.what: Open-gripper sweep: hovered and descended with the open fingers straddling the print (tilt 20 deg, yaw -120 deg, closing axis along -30 deg, tips ~3 mm above the plate), then swept 14 cm along -30 deg, yaw turning to -105 deg.
steps.why: A slow push needs only a small force, so the arm's compliance shouldn't let the rear finger ride up; this pose family was reachable and clear of the column.
steps.result: Steps 475-633. The rear finger pushed the print off the plate's front edge. It ended tipped between the plate edge and the shelf, centre x~0.18.

steps.what: Pushed 4 cm further in +x, 6 mm lower.
steps.why: Get the print fully onto the shelf instead of bridging the plate edge.
steps.result: Step 659. The print stands on one of its hex side faces on the shelf top, at the shelf's back edge.

steps.what: Retreated: a straight-up move was unreachable, so I moved up 4 cm while drawing 3 cm toward the base, yaw -90 deg. Then checked both cameras, the cloud, and the plate.
steps.why: Clear the gripper without touching the print, then verify.
steps.result: Step 693. Print on the shelf: lowest point z 0.066 (shelf top 0.065), centre ~(0.20, -0.424), inside the shelf footprint, standing on edge and leaning toward the plate's front edge. Plate unmoved (z 0.0845, same footprint). Called finish_episode.

key_images.caption: Start, left camera: printer, black plate with the orange hex print, black shelf in front.
Perception ids at the start: obj5 print, obj4 plate, obj6 shelf, obj1-3 printer.
Top-down render of the print's points with the fitted hexagon (red).
First descent: gripper 1 cm off-centre (joint deadband), one finger against the print.
After the deadband-compensated re-centring: fingers straddle the print evenly.
Close 1: the fingers rode over the print and closed on air (0.9685).
Close 2 (15 deg tilt): fingers on top, pinching the blue disc (gap 1.86 cm).
Test lift: the print tilts up on one side, then the pinch slips.
Open gripper straddling the print, tips near the plate, before the sweep.
After the 14 cm sweep: the print pushed off the plate edge, tipped at the plate/shelf boundary.
Final, left camera: print on the shelf's back edge, standing on a side face; plate in place.
Final, right camera: print on the black shelf top next to the plate edge; gripper clear.

diagnosis: The print ended on the black shelf and the plate never moved, but I'm not certain this scores as a success. The print is not lying flat: it stands on one hex side face at the shelf's back edge (lowest point at shelf height, centre about 3 cm inside the shelf's back edge), leaning toward the plate's front edge. It may touch the plate or printer edge. If the scorer wants the print resting flat, clearly inside the shelf, or touching nothing but the shelf, this fails. Root cause: grasping failed. In both closes (25 and 15 deg tilt) the fingertips rode up over the 1.4 cm part as the jaws squeezed: TCP +5.6 mm and +3.1 mm. This points to a chamfered or curved fingertip pad plus vertical compliance in the arm. The second close only pinched the 2.3 mm disc, which could not carry the print's weight. Pushing from behind was blocked by the printer column, and a drag via the disc pinch slipped. The open-gripper sweep worked, but it dropped the print over the plate's 2 cm step, where it landed on edge, and my second push stood it upright rather than laying it flat. I spent ~25 min and ~250 steps on grasp attempts before switching to the sweep, which left no time to tidy the final pose. Next time: try one close at the lowest safe height early, and as soon as the fingers ride up, switch to sweeping. Sweep further, in one continuous motion that lowers the rear finger after the plate edge, so the print slides fully onto the shelf. Then, if it lands on edge, topple it flat by pushing its top edge from the plate side, and finish nearer the shelf centre.
lessons: This sim PiPER's joints stop a fixed amount short of their target in the direction of motion (about 0.003-0.007 rad on joints 1-4 and 0.030 rad on joints 5-6, no settling while holding). Commanding FK(q_goal + dead*sign(q_goal - q_now)) cut the TCP error from 6-10 mm to under 0.5 mm.

The real fingertips reach ~2.45 cm past the TCP (measured in the point cloud), not the nominal 2.0 cm. With a tilted approach the low finger corner sits 2.5-2.7 cm below the TCP. Measure it from the cloud before going near a surface.

These fingers cannot squeeze-grasp a part ~1.4 cm tall lying on a surface: the tips ride up over its top edge as the jaws close, whatever the tilt (15 or 25 deg). For such low parts, plan a push or sweep from the start.

A slow sweep with the open gripper straddling the part (closing axis along the push, tips a few mm above the surface) moved the print reliably. The small pushing force doesn't make the fingers ride up the way the gripper's squeeze does.

Near the printer column, top-down poses at ~37 cm radius hit joint5's 1.22 rad limit and the forearm hits the column. Tilting the approach ~15-25 deg toward azimuth -120..-145 deg (wrist shifted toward +x) solved both.
The point cloud includes the robot's own body, so clearance computed against the cloud is polluted near the arm's current pose. Use check()/check_batch() (robot removed) there.
When pushing a part off a raised plate onto a lower shelf, sweep far enough that it clears the step, or follow up to lay it flat; otherwise it can land on edge against the step.
